text: The subject, Hina Shah, a freelance software developer with a declared monthly income of PKR 90,000, received a series of high‑value inbound IBFT transfers from a large number of unrelated counterparties between 1 May and 10 May 2026. In the 14‑day window she received six deposits exceeding PKR 45,000 (PKR 45,000, PKR 61,000, PKR 49,000, PKR 63,000, PKR 49,000 and PKR 41,000) from different individuals and banks, amounting to more than PKR 300,000. Within hours of the last inbound deposit, the account transferred PKR 165,000 on 8 May and PKR 86,000 on 11 May to a QuickPay e‑wallet (WLT****0932) via wallet‑transfer channels. The outbound amounts represent a large share of the inbound value and were moved to a wallet that is not linked to the subject’s declared business or personal needs. The typology engine flagged the activity (score 360) for “many distinct inbound counterparties in 14 days” and “large share of inbound value leaves quickly”, exceeding the alert threshold. The rapid conversion of numerous unrelated deposits into a single e‑wallet suggests the account is being used as a “border mule” to funnel illicit funds, warranting a Suspicious Transaction Report.
